name: struct-array-scan
axis: array of structs scanned by field — memory layout (inline records vs array of references)
n: n=2000000 four-field records built once, then r=100 scan passes = 200M element visits (one unconditional field read, one predicated pair)
notes: This is the layout benchmark. Rust's `Vec<Rec>` stores the records INLINE — 16 bytes each, ~4 per cache line, one contiguous stream with hardware prefetch. VL's `Rec[]`, JS's array-of-objects and Python's list-of-objects are all arrays of REFERENCES: one pointer chase per element into a separately allocated cell. VL has no way to ask for the inline layout. opt.vl shows the size of that gap by hand-exploding the record into four parallel `i32[]` columns (struct-of-arrays) — the layout Rust gets for free — at the cost of the `Rec` type ceasing to exist. Scale-verified: r doubling gives 1.75-2.00x for rust/vl/deno (sub-2.0 because the 2M-record build phase is fixed); Python's r was raised to 20 for the same reason.
